primary_question: When repeated phenotypes recur, are they regenerated by reactivation of retained ancestral developmental programs rather than repeated de novo invention?

decisions.REACTIVATION_STRONG: ancestral state, persistence, suppression and homologous reactivation supported; alternative mechanisms excluded; perturbation/rescue strongly preferred
decisions.REACTIVATION_SUPPORTIVE: persistence, suppression and homologous re-expression supported without direct causal rescue
decisions.STANDING_VARIATION_RELEASE: cryptic/standing alleles explain recurrence without demonstrated continuity of one suppressed ancestral program
decisions.INTROGRESSIVE_REACQUISITION: relevant state/program is reacquired through reticulation
decisions.DE_NOVO_PARALLELISM: independent new changes recreate phenotype without retained ancestral-program continuity
decisions.NON_HOMOLOGOUS_RECONSTRUCTION: ancestral-like phenotype uses a different generative route

nature_hierarchy.headline: module_boundary_evolvability / reconfigurable inheritance
nature_hierarchy.downstream_mechanism: latent ancestral program reactivation is one explanation for repeated component availability
nature_hierarchy.forbidden_substitution: a reactivation result cannot rescue a failed F/M/R inheritance-unit test
